decisions.reason: As a flagship product closely tied to the firm's sustainability and reusable-packaging direction, its upside is still uncertain but promising, so the option value of keeping it is high relative to near-term carrying cost.

A foldable large-container line fits the firm's core logistics-packaging business and its own dedicated page suggests meaningful commitment, so management would likely keep this option open while market acceptance develops.

Although a stackable plastic crate is strategically related to the core business, it appears less prominently positioned and is in a more standard category, so it has a somewhat higher drop risk but is still worth retaining this early.

The medium-duty rackable pallet line is aligned with the firm's established pallet offering, but because it was only mentioned and not highlighted, management would keep it for now while recognizing a comparatively higher chance of later rationalization.
The spill-retention pallet line has a clear industrial use case and dedicated presentation, so for a large manufacturer it remains a reasonable option to hold while demand uncertainty resolves.

This plastic pallet with load retainers complements the firm's reusable transport portfolio and had enough visibility to justify continued market presence, though it is not central enough to make drop risk negligible.
